## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `873d3a6d0edb6e11a79b527ac98040a35d753b67`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md,scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs + none
Security-touching: yes

First record on PR #37939 for card #37782. Read: the card body and its five comments (triage 7208787937, claim 7217183680, dev reports 7217962987, 7218940982 and its correction 7218957386); the PR title, body and 3-file list; the net diff against `origin/main` `bc173343` (+17/-6); the 49 check-runs on the head (31 success, 18 skipped, none failed). Nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run. Git objects were read in place (`git show`, `wc -c`, and `git merge-tree --write-tree`, which writes no worktree). The head's first parent line already contains `bc173343`: the merge base is current `origin/main` itself, and the merge-tree of the two is the head's own tree `fb60f171`, so "the head merged with current origin/main" is the head, byte for byte.

`Security-touching: yes`, conservatively. The words this PR changes teach schema refusal only. But the changed `agent.tools` line carries, unchanged, the sentence on tool reach ("resolved names against the *full* registry with no surface check"), and the same hunk holds the `agent.knowledge` row on where retrieval is restricted (`aiExposed`, `source.where`). Record 7218120173 on PR #37797 marked the same table `yes` for that reason. Both statements are `main`'s text and still true; nothing security-relevant is newly taught. The seat decides the label.

### ① Derived judgments

- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`: one hunk, 5 lines for 5. The paragraph above the retired-key table, the header cell, and one clause of the `agent.tools` row. Published skill prose only. Right.
- `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: one row, 6795 to 6791, plus one comment line. A lowering to the measurement; no ceiling rises, no other row moves. Right.
- `.changeset/37782-ai-skill-retired-agent-keys-refusal.md`: new, `@objectstack/skills` patch. Right.
- No spec schema, no accept set of a published type, no runtime code, no eval file and no test changes. `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/` is `main`'s bytes. The accept set of `AgentSchema` is untouched: the text now describes the refusal `main` already issues.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` patch matches what the diff publishes: corrected prose in one shipped skill file. `Check Changeset` is green on the head (both runs).

Clause-②: no. Correct on the PR body and in the changeset: nothing an author could write before is refused now, and nothing refused before is accepted. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

The changeset, sentence by sentence against `main`:
- Title, "describes the refusal the two retired agent keys get today": true.
- "called `agent.tools` and `agent.knowledge` tombstones whose parse error carries its migration, and cited two line numbers of `agent.zod.ts` that no longer point at either key": true. `main`'s paragraph says exactly that, and `agent.zod.ts` on `main` has a type export near :234 and the `LONG_TERM_STORE_RETIRED` constant at :251; `AgentSchema` (:339) declares neither key and no `retiredKey()` for either.
- "Both tombstones left the schema in protocol 18": true (`agent.test.ts:102-103`, "left the shape at 18 (#25767, ADR-0087 D2 = A)"; :233, "aged out at 18 with its kit").
- "it refuses each as an unknown key, and the refusal names https://objectstack.ai/docs/protocol-upgrade": true, see ④.
- "The table header says the same in short": close enough; the header gives the two dates, not the refusal.
- "the clause that said a migration deletes the key and names each listed tool now says the strict schema refuses the key as unknown": true.
- "the conversion that did that left the load path in 17.0.0": true as a fact, see N1.
- "The replacements both rows teach are unchanged, and the file is 4 tokens shorter": true, see ④.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 7217962987, open question (cite the strict-object refusal in words, option A, or add the `agent.test.ts` path and pay for it elsewhere, option B): answered A. The card's own wording is "cite the test or the strict-object refusal, not stale line numbers", an either-or, and the paragraph takes the second arm: it names the strict schema and the unknown-key refusal. That is enough. The card's acceptance line asks that every `agent.zod.ts` / `agent.test.ts` citation in the section match `main`; the section now holds none, so nothing is left to drift. The reader of a published skill is an author or an authoring model outside this repository, for whom the upgrade-guide URL is the usable pointer and a spec test path is not. The pinning tests are named in the PR body for the reviewer, which is where they belong.
- Dev reports 7218940982 and 7218957386: `open_questions` empty.
- Dev note, PR body still describing round 1: answered. The body read at this head describes round 2 (the clause, 6795 to 6791, three files).
- Carry from record 7218120173 and L1 7218142210 on PR #37797 (card #37782 names the paragraph and the header, not the clause inside the `agent.tools` row, so this PR must cover the clause explicitly): discharged. The clause is rewritten, and the PR body, the changeset and the ratchet note each name it. The claim's file surface (7217183680) said the two rows stay untouched; the widening to one clause of one row is the carry those two records ordered, not drift.
- Declared overlap (7218957386): PR #37947, PR #37937 and PR #36158 each conflict with this branch in `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`, at the lowered row, and nowhere else. Read at the object level for the first two (heads `d7c3960e`, `f008bf4c`): the only conflicted path is the ratchet script, and `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` auto-merges. PR #36158's file list holds the ratchet script and not this skill file; its merge was not computed here, so its conflict stands as the dev's reading. No finding: the row is a measurement, and whichever lands second merges `main` and re-measures. The seat should land this PR knowing the other three then owe that re-measure.
- CI: 31 success, 18 skipped, none failed, among them `Type Check · source gates`, the `Lint` families, `Test Core`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, id materialisation or join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`** against the spec on `main` `bc173343`. The card names no eval prompt; its acceptance is the citations and the skills gates.

The paragraph, fact by fact:
- "Two `AgentSchema` keys are retired, not legacy options": true. `AgentSchema` (`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts:339`) is built with `strictObject`; its shape declares no `tools` and no `knowledge`, and its `aliases` and `guidance` maps name neither.
- "the strict schema refuses each as an unknown key": true for both. `tools`: `agent.test.ts:101-114`, "REFUSES a legacy inline tools array as an unknown key naming the upgrade guide". `knowledge`: `agent.test.ts:232-242`, which asserts `unrecognized_keys` and the key name.
- "naming https://objectstack.ai/docs/protocol-upgrade", and the word "each": true for BOTH keys, not `tools` alone. :114 matches the key `tools` followed by the URL; :242 asserts the same URL for `knowledge`. The reason it holds for any unknown key on this schema: `strictUnknownKeyError` appends `RETIRED_KEY_UPGRADE_GUIDE_SENTENCE` unless a surface opts out with `retiredKeyUpgradeGuide: false` (`packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts:383-386`), and `AgentSchema` does not opt out. The URL is `PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_GUIDE_URL` (`packages/spec/src/shared/protocol-upgrade-guide.ts:23`), spelled identically in the skill.
- Header, "Removed in 17, tombstone gone in 18": true. Removed in 17: `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx:205` and `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx:311-312` on `main` (#3894, #3896), and the protocol-17 step's rationale in `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`. Gone in 18: the two test comments cited under ②, and the kit rule in `protocol-upgrade-guide.ts` (a retirement kit lives one major past its retirement, then the key is an ordinary unknown key).

The `agent.tools` row. The clause "the strict schema refuses the key as unknown" is now true, by the same test (:101-114). The clause it replaces had become false: `agent-tools-to-skills` is in no conversion registry or entry module on `main` (`packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/17/` holds one file, the sharing-rule one); the id survives only in `CHANGELOG.md` and in `retired-after.census.json`, whose `retired` list carries it from release 17.0.0 on (first at :74, absent from the 16.1.0 block). The rest of both rows against PR #37797's landed text: `main` has not touched the file since `3247e87d`, and the diff against `main` changes, inside the two rows, only that clause and one word, "re-declare each" to "re-declare each tool", needed because the antecedent "each tool that was listed" left with the old clause. The why-sentence of the `agent.tools` row, its replacement (`defineSkill` under the stack's `skills`, ADR-0064) and the whole `agent.knowledge` row are byte-identical to `3247e87d`.

Tried to break it: an author who writes either key gets a refusal that names the key and the URL the paragraph gives, so the text predicts the real message. The row now repeats the paragraph's refusal in six words; redundant, not wrong, and the file still shrank.

**`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`**, the one hunk:
- 6795 to 6791: confirmed by byte count, without running the gate. The script's convention is `ceil(utf8 bytes / 4)` with the release-stamp line excluded. The file is 27191 bytes on the head and 27207 on `main`; the stamp line is 27 bytes on both; 27164 / 4 = 6791 exactly, and 27180 / 4 = 6795 for `main`. The head is `main` plus this PR, so the merged tree measures 6791. Headroom 0, a lowering only. `Type Check · source gates` is green on the head.
- Comment, the transition 6795 to 6791, tagged #37782: true, both numbers verified.
- "the `agent.tools` row no longer teaches an aged-out migration": true; the conversion aged out with its kit, as shown above. The paragraph and header edits are byte-neutral (244 bytes before and after, round-1 report), so the 16 bytes do come from the row.
- "LOWERED to the measurement": true.
- The notes `main` wrote above the row and the row's trailing note are untouched. No other row moves.

N1 (nit) — the changeset says the old clause is stale because "the conversion that did that left the load path in 17.0.0". The census confirms the fact, but it is not the cause: the protocol-17 step says its tombstoned conversions were `retiredFromLoadPath` "from the day they land", and through 17.x `os migrate meta --from 16` still deleted the key and named each tool. What made the clause false is that the conversion aged out with its retirement kit at 18 (#25767). The ratchet note's "aged-out migration" has it right. Changeset prose only; accepted as is.

N2 (nit) — outside the diff: `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`, case 5, `expected_output` still says `agent.tools` / `agent.knowledge` "are protocol-17 tombstones", which the skill no longer says and `main`'s schema no longer does. The case's machine assertions (`must_contain`, `must_not_contain`) do not depend on that wording, so its verdict does not move. Follow-up card for the eval prose, not this PR: the eval file is outside the card's surface and editing it reopens case 5's round.

N3 (nit) — outside the diff, same follow-up: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx:311-312` still teaches both keys as "typed `never`", the tombstone behaviour that left at 18, and the comment at `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts:100` still says `agent.knowledge` is "tombstoned below". The PR body already notes the drifted `agent.zod.ts:87-95` citation in the skill's Model Configuration section.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

## 维护者速读

- 做什么：AI 技能文档里讲两个已退役 agent 字段的那段，原来说「写了会报错并附迁移提示」，还引用了两个早已对不上的源码行号。现在改成如实描述：schema 会把它们当未知字段拒绝，报错里给出升级指南链接；表头也改为「17 移除，18 起连提示也去掉」。
- 风险：3 个文件 +17/−6，只改文档文字，长度上限往下调 4。没有代码、协议或运行时变化；教的替代写法不变。
- 要你做什么：审批人批准即可，契约审核 PASS 评论 7219261608，Head-sha `873d3a6d0edb6e11a79b527ac98040a35d753b67`；批准后座位自主落地。
- 不批会怎样：文档继续描述已经不存在的报错方式和行号，照着排查的人会找不到对应代码。

Seat opinion: land.
